newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former Australian premier to challenge Hanson.
newsitem.headline: Former Australian premier to challenge Hanson.

text.p: A former Australian state premier on Monday said he would challenge controversial politician Pauline Hanson at the ballot box at the next general election.

Wayne Goss, former Queensland state premier and one of the opposition Australian Labor Party's most successful political stars, announced his challenge after news that Hanson's electorate was likely to be reshaped.
The planned electoral changes would see Hanson's seat of Oxley dominated by staunch Labor voters. Labor easily held the seat until Hanson's victory in March 1996.

"I'm happy to run against her. I believe that as the Labor candidate, I can win," said Goss, who ended more than 20 years of conservative rule in Queensland when he became state premier in 1989, a position he held until early 1996.

Under the Australian Electoral Commission's draft redistribution of electoral boundaries in Queensland, Hanson's seat on the western fringe of the state capital, Brisbane, would gain some of Australia's strongest pro-Labor territory while losing some conservative areas.
The new boundaries include the area where Goss grew up.
Treasurer Peter Costello urged Hanson to battle Goss and test the popularity of her controversial anti-immigration views.
"I think Pauline Hanson should run and test her electoral strength," Costello said in a radio interview.

Goss still faces a selection process by the Labor Party and is likely to be challenged by at least one other Labor hopeful. The general election is due by May 1999, although it is widely expected to be called late next year.
Hanson sparked a divisive national race row last year when she warned Australia was in danger of being swamped by Asians and criticised welfare for native Aborigines.

Her One Nation Party has attracted substantial support, but also violent and rowdy protests. The party averages about seven percent in opinion polls, making it potentially the third force behind the Liberal-National government and Labor.
